text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] KV-prefetch amplification spike detected · us-west-2 · dashboards alert fired · 3.2x baseline CPU on kv-proxy cluster

emma (oncall): paging - I'm on it. seeing steep tail latency for a subset of tenants, looks correlated with continuous-batching prefetches.

raj (eng-runtime): on my way. logs show repeated prefetch miss storms + eviction churn. suspect prefetch window too wide for some customers after last rollout.

lina (sre): impact summary from metrics: 12% of requests in last 10m hit >500ms token latency, 24 customers with >5% error increase. SLA alerts triggered for 3 customers (acme-inc, glowai, papertrail).

maria (support): looping in account teams. acme-inc on support call — they report degraded response times and occasional 503s.

toshi (eng-infra): quick check: no node restarts, but host CPU on kv-shard-7 at 96%. KV eviction rate up 6x.

emma (oncall): can we scale? is this safe to autoscale?

raj (eng-runtime): autoscale would help but replication will just move eviction problem. safer to narrow prefetch window + enable per-customer batching limit. preparing a config patch.

raj (eng-runtime): patch payload (will canary to 10% of traffic first):

```
PATCH /config/global
{
  "continuous_batching": {
    "prefetch_enabled": true,
    "prefetch_window_ms": 50,   # lowered from 200
    "per_customer_max_prefetch": 8
  }
}
```

emma (oncall): can we add a per-tenant override for the 24 affected customers while we validate?

raj (eng-runtime): yes. per-tenant override config looks like: `overrides[tenant_id].continuous_batching.prefetch_window_ms=10` — I'll prepare a list.

maria (support): sending tenant list now: acme-inc, glowai, papertrail, zeta-labs, medlytics, starlane, lexprint, novus-ai, datum-ops, ripplepay, 14 others...

lina (sre): estimate impact if we flip to prefetch_window_ms=50 globally and per-tenant=10 for affected: expected CPU drop ~40% in kv-proxy and latency should return to baseline for non-affected tenants.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout: config/continuous-batcher v3 -> canary(10%) -> targets: kv-proxy-us-west-2-a,b; rollout tracked by /ops/releases/2487654321

emma (oncall): monitor logs for amplification loops; if eviction rate doesn't drop in 5m we revert.

raj (eng-runtime): canary metrics: first 3 minutes look good — eviction rate down 55% on canary nodes. CPU down 48%.

toshi (eng-infra): ok to expand to 50%?

raj (eng-runtime): expand to 50% now. increasing canary scope.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary expanded: 50% -> kv-proxy-us-west-2-a,b,c,d; auto-checking health.

maria (support): acme-inc reports improvement on call, latency dropping. sending update to customer #inc-3482.

lina (sre): watch for secondary effects: burstiness can shift to downstream model pools. tracing shows slight spike in model-queue length for tenant 'novus-ai' around the canary nodes, keeping an eye.

emma (oncall): schedule per-tenant overrides for the 24 customers immediately — avoid blanket time windows. raj, can you commit the overrides?

raj (eng-runtime): committing overrides now. snippet applied: `overrides:{"acme-inc":{prefetch_window_ms:10,per_customer_max_prefetch:4}, ...}`. pushing config v3.1.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: overrides applied to tenant set (24 ids). verification monitor active.

toshi (eng-infra): infrastructure note: we also tightened KV slab eviction thresholds on canary hosts to avoid oscillation: `kv.slab.eviction_alpha=0.7` (was 0.5).

lina (sre): overall cluster CPU down to 65% of previous peak. per-tenant errors reduced to baseline for 19/24 tenants, 5 still elevated but improving.

emma (oncall): which 5?

maria (support): still elevated: glowai, novus-ai, ripplepay, starlane, datum-ops. Customer contacts notified, assigned follow-ups.

raj (eng-runtime): next step for the remaining 5: schedule targeted micro-canaries with per-tenant window 5ms and throttle max_prefetch=2, and enable short-term requeue backoff. I'll prepare a patch.

emma (oncall): do we need to open an incident retro ticket? seems like rollout tuning caused regression for medium-high qps tenants.

lina (sre): yes - assign postmortem to eng-runtime + infra. tag with RCA hypothesis: prefetch window default too permissive for skewed tenant traffic patterns; missing per-tenant rate limits in initial rollout.

ops-bot: incident-bot: incident STATE=mitigated -> summary posted to /incidents/2487654321. create-retro issue created: ENG-2487.

raj (eng-runtime): rolling micro-canaries for the 5 remaining now. applying per-tenant window 5ms; throttle 2.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: micro-canaries applied, monitoring.

lina (sre): all metrics back to normal for the remaining tenants after 7m. eviction rates stable, no secondary failures. closing active mitigation.

maria (support): all impacted customers updated, support tickets moving to monitoring; acme-inc removed from SLA alert.

emma (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall. notes attached to thread and incident doc: timeline, config diffs, tenant list, follow-ups (postmortem + guardrails).

raj (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add pre-deploy simulation for prefetch defaults, add per-tenant safety caps in codepath, and add metric that alerts when eviction_rate increases >2x within 5m.

lina (sre): agreed. also add a temporary dashboard tile for prefetch amplification ratio per-tenant.

emma (oncall): thanks team. I'll mark this as resolved but keep incident doc open for retro. :thumbsup:
